lesson_title: Formulas Are Machines: Run Them Both Ways
hook_text: One wrong button and your car hire costs R157 250. Here's the button.
clip_script: Now compute — and here stands the great trap of forward substitution: the order of operations. Multiplication before addition, always. The wrong road adds first: 450 plus 12,50 gives 462,50, times 340 gives a monstrous R157 250 — a hire-car bill that buys the car. The right road multiplies first. So: 12,50 times 340 gives 4 250. Then add the fixed charge: 450 plus 4 250 equals 4 700. The 340 kilometre trip costs R4 700. Sense-check it against the story: the trip charge should dwarf the entrance fee on a long drive. Reasonable.
visual_style: Split-screen calculator race: the wrong keystroke order exploding into a giant red R157 250, the correct order landing calmly on R4 700 with a green tick.
pacing: Fast disaster reveal, slower correct walkthrough, snappy sense-check close.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and learn to run the formula backwards too.
